evaluations.evidence: create a new game
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes complementary capabilities for games (invite/join, run rounds, browse/view/export/delete), so game creation is not a missing step.

evaluations.evidence: invite estimators by giving them a URL
evaluations.rationale: Complementary capability exists for estimators to use the URL to join the game.

evaluations.evidence: start a round by entering an item
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes viewing/selecting items and participant-side viewing/estimating, so starting a round is supported by complementary steps.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Items can be created/added/imported and selected, so listing them is not missing a prerequisite capability.

evaluations.evidence: select an item to be estimated or re-estimated
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes ways to create/add items and to re-estimate earlier items, so selection has the needed complementary capabilities.

evaluations.evidence: add an item to the list of items
evaluations.rationale: Complementary CRUD capabilities exist (edit/delete/view/select), so item creation is not an incomplete set.

evaluations.evidence: edit an item in the list
evaluations.rationale: Editing presupposes item existence; backlog includes item creation/import/copy-paste, satisfying the complementary prerequisite.

evaluations.evidence: delete an item from the list
evaluations.rationale: Deletion presupposes item existence; backlog includes multiple ways to create/add items, so no missing complementary capability.

evaluations.evidence: show all estimates immediately
evaluations.rationale: Backlog lacks any story that lets participants actually submit/play an estimate (choose a card). Showing estimates (immediately or after all) requires estimate creation/submission capability.

evaluations.evidence: accept the average of all estimates
evaluations.rationale: Accepting an average requires that estimates exist; backlog does not include a story for participants to submit an estimate/card, so the necessary complementary capability is missing.

evaluations.evidence: if all estimators show the same card
evaluations.rationale: Auto-filling based on shown cards requires the ability for estimators to play/show a card (submit an estimate), which is not present as a story in the backlog.

evaluations.evidence: enter the agreed-upon estimate
evaluations.rationale: Entering a final estimate can stand alone as moderator input and is complemented by transcript/export stories that use stored estimates.

evaluations.evidence: estimate a story we estimated earlier ... again
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes selecting items for re-estimation and viewing prior rounds, providing complementary support for re-estimation flow.

evaluations.evidence: import stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Imported stories complement the item list/selection/edit/delete capabilities; no missing prerequisite is implied.

evaluations.evidence: copy/paste stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Copy/paste provides another creation path for items and is complemented by item management stories.

evaluations.evidence: browse through previous games
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes game creation and viewing/exporting transcripts, so browsing previous games has complementary creation and read capabilities.

evaluations.evidence: view a transcript of a game
evaluations.rationale: Transcript viewing is complemented by game creation and estimate/item capture stories (items and agreed estimates), and export stories build on transcript existence.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript ... as a HTML file
evaluations.rationale: Export presupposes transcript existence; backlog includes viewing transcripts, satisfying the complementary prerequisite.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript ... as a CSV file
evaluations.rationale: Export presupposes transcript existence; backlog includes viewing transcripts, satisfying the complementary prerequisite.

evaluations.evidence: delete a game
evaluations.rationale: Deletion presupposes game existence; backlog includes game creation and browsing/viewing, so complementary capabilities exist.

evaluations.evidence: create an account
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes login, change details, delete account, and password reminder, forming a reasonably complete account lifecycle.

evaluations.evidence: log in using my account name and password
evaluations.rationale: Login is complemented by account creation and password reminder, so crucial prerequisites are present.

evaluations.evidence: change my account details
evaluations.rationale: Changing details presupposes an account; backlog includes account creation and login, satisfying complementary prerequisites.

evaluations.evidence: delete my account
evaluations.rationale: Account deletion presupposes account existence; backlog includes account creation and login, so complementary capabilities exist.

evaluations.evidence: see dates and times in my local timezone
evaluations.rationale: This is an application-wide display capability and does not expose a missing complementary CRUD step in the backlog.

evaluations.evidence: get a password reminder by email
evaluations.rationale: Password reminder is complemented by account creation and login; no additional necessary story is implied for completeness at backlog level.

evaluations.evidence: select whether to have the team estimate with {0, 1/2, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, etc.} or {0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, etc.}
evaluations.rationale: Deck selection is a configuration feature and does not reveal a missing complementary capability beyond the core estimating flow (handled elsewhere).

evaluations.evidence: invite up to 15 estimators
evaluations.rationale: This refines inviting; complementary join capability exists.

evaluations.evidence: join a game ... I received the URL for
evaluations.rationale: Joining via URL is complemented by moderator invitation via URL.

evaluations.evidence: see the item we're estimating
evaluations.rationale: Item visibility is complemented by moderator creating/starting/selecting items.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we will try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Participant list view is complemented by moderator item creation/import and list management.

evaluations.evidence: see that an estimate has been given by a specific estimator
evaluations.rationale: This requires the ability for an estimator to give/submit an estimate; backlog has no explicit story for submitting an estimate/card, so a crucial complementary capability is missing.

evaluations.evidence: after all estimators have given their estimate
evaluations.rationale: Showing all estimates after everyone has given one presupposes a capability for estimators to submit an estimate; no such creation/submission story exists.

evaluations.evidence: be able to change my estimate
evaluations.rationale: Changing an estimate presupposes that an estimate can be made/submitted in the first place; backlog lacks an explicit estimate submission story.

evaluations.evidence: see each estimator's prior estimates for the story being estimated
evaluations.rationale: Viewing prior estimates presupposes that estimates are captured per estimator; backlog lacks an explicit story for estimators to submit estimates, creating a completeness gap.

evaluations.evidence: see who gave what estimates during the current round
evaluations.rationale: Requires that participants can submit estimates and that the system records them; estimate submission is not covered by any story.

evaluations.evidence: start a two-minute countdown timer that all participants can see
evaluations.rationale: Timer functionality is self-contained and does not imply a missing complementary CRUD capability elsewhere in the backlog.

evaluations.evidence: reset itself as soon as we all play an estimate
evaluations.rationale: Automatic reset condition depends on the capability for participants to play/submit an estimate; that complementary capability is missing from the backlog.

evaluations.evidence: scroll back through the stories and estimates from prior rounds
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes creating items and recording agreed estimates (moderator entry) and viewing transcripts, supporting the existence of prior-round data to scroll through.

evaluations.evidence: cards in the same order across multiple draws
evaluations.rationale: Card ordering is a UI consistency feature and does not expose a missing complementary capability in the backlog.

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate as long as the draw has not been completed
evaluations.rationale: Changing an estimate requires that an estimate can be submitted in the first place; backlog lacks an explicit story for submitting/playing an estimate.

evaluations.evidence: have a small thumbnail photo displayed near where my cards are played
evaluations.rationale: Displaying a participant photo presupposes a way to provide/upload/set that photo; no story covers supplying participant photos, so a complementary capability is missing.

evaluations.evidence: compliant with XHTML and CSS standards
evaluations.rationale: This is a non-functional requirement and does not imply missing complementary functional steps for feature completeness.

evaluations.evidence: have a list of definitions for commonly used terms
evaluations.rationale: Glossary/documentation is self-contained and does not expose a missing complementary capability required by other stories.

evaluations.evidence: created database indexes
evaluations.rationale: Implementation detail/performance support does not require complementary CRUD stories for completeness.

evaluations.evidence: function correctly in Internet Explorer 6 and 7, Firefox 1.5 and 2, and Safari 2
evaluations.rationale: Compatibility NFR does not expose missing complementary functional capabilities in the backlog.

evaluations.evidence: comply with the W3C accessibility guidelines
evaluations.rationale: Accessibility NFR does not imply missing complementary functional steps for feature completeness.

evaluations.evidence: respond quickly to my actions
evaluations.rationale: Performance NFR does not create a complementary functional gap under the completeness criterion.

evaluations.evidence: be able to use Unicode
evaluations.rationale: Internationalization support is cross-cutting and does not expose a missing complementary functional capability in the backlog.

evaluations.evidence: see sensible and predictable URLs
evaluations.rationale: URL design is cross-cutting and does not imply missing complementary CRUD/flow steps.

evaluations.evidence: nice error pages when something goes wrong
evaluations.rationale: Error page handling is self-contained and does not reveal a missing complementary functional capability required by other stories.

evaluations.evidence: results to be stored in a non-identifiable way
evaluations.rationale: Non-identifiable storage for research presupposes a capability to access/export/analyze those stored results for research; backlog has no researcher-facing story to retrieve the anonymized dataset/metrics, leaving a complementary capability missing for this research feature.

evaluations.evidence: see some metrics on use of the game
evaluations.rationale: Metrics require that usage events/results are captured and stored in a way suitable for reporting; backlog does not include explicit instrumentation/usage logging or a defined data capture story to support metrics generation.
